clue.text: Means of laundering cash, when aiming high?

indicators.note: someone high is intoxicated, out of their normal state, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A wry question: is money-laundering about aiming high, a crook's ambition dressed as a household gadget?
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' scrambles the fourteen letters of CASH WHEN AIMING. The answer runs across two lights, 1 and 5 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic appliance that cleans clothes is a device for laundering them, the literal sense of the clue's word.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-wells perhaps said little after dropping ecstasy

parts.note: said was, in the sense of 'was terse' meaning spoke briefly; the phrase said little is was terse

indicators.note: dropping says a letter is let fall from the phrase just found

parts.note: with said, little gives terse: someone terse says little
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Layabouts who went quiet once they came off the drug.
explanation.walkthrough: WAS TERSE loses one E, its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasters are idle good-for-nothings, the same people the old phrase ne'er-do-wells describes.

clue.text: Very grave case of leprosy

parts.note: a grave matter is a serious one

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A doctor's verdict on a dreadful instance of leprosy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very grave' reads as one phrase, but 'Very' alone is the definition. 'case of' keeps the outer L and Y of 'leprosy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seriously works as an intensifier, as in seriously good, meaning extremely.

clue.text: Has-been's admission that makes progress impossible

parts.note: the admission is I'M, a speaker owning up to what they are
a has-been is passé, out of date and no longer fashionable

explanation.surface: A washed-up figure's confession that they can go no further.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the has-been's admission aloud as I'M PASSÉ and the answer appears.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock, a stalemate in which no further advance can be made.

clue.text: Style of dress ends in small size 8

parts.note: garb is clothing, a manner of dress

indicators.note: the ends of each of the two following words are their last letters

explanation.surface: A fashion note about a small size 8 garment.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' looks like a dress size but is a cross-reference to 8 down, ENCRYPT. 'ends in' takes L and E from 'small' and 'size'.
explanation.definitionFit: To garble a message is to scramble it so it cannot be understood, much as encoding it does.

clue.text: See 1
Stomach releasing tense, nervous reactions initially could produce butterflies

indicators.note: could produce suggests the letters may be worked into something new
releasing means letting a letter go from the word before it

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Nerves before a big moment: the stomach fluttering, the classic butterflies.
explanation.walkthrough: STOMACH without T gives SOMACH; add N and R and rearrange, as 'could produce' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchs are a well-known species of large orange migratory butterfly.

clue.text: Establishments that sell better chips

parts.note: a better here is one who bets, and gaming chips are sold to gamblers, not fried potatoes to diners

explanation.surface: Restaurants or chip shops boasting superior fries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as an adjective but is a person who bets; the chips are gaming tokens.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambling houses exchange money for tokens that punters then stake at the tables.

clue.text: Interior designer regularly developed new lines

indicators.note: developed says the letters are worked up into a new arrangement
regularly takes every other letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An interior designer has come up with a fresh range of products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives EINR from 'designer'; add N and 'developed' rearranges them. 'lines' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner and interior are both adjectives for what lies inside, so one substitutes for the other.

clue.text: Gateway computer's T&C changed and put into unintelligible form

indicators.note: T&C changed tells us those two particular letters change places

parts.note: a gateway is an entry, a way in
PC is a personal computer

explanation.surface: Gateway, a computer maker, rewrote its terms and conditions into impenetrable legalese.
explanation.walkthrough: ENTRY PC has its T and C swapped, as 'T&C changed' instructs, giving the answer. T&C usually means terms and conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Encrypting data scrambles it into a code nobody can read without the key.

clue.text: Material not fit for use in Fight Club

parts.note: a scrap is an informal word for a fight
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Something unsuitable to be used in the film Fight Club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fight Club' reads as the film's title, but splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap iron is discarded metal, waste fit only for melting down rather than use.

clue.text: 6 missing when coming back travelling at the speed of sound

definitions.text: travelling at the speed of sound

indicators.note: coming back says what remains is read in reverse
missing says those letters are absent from the word

parts.note: 6 refers to the answer of 6 down, CASINOS
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Something missing when returning at supersonic speed.
explanation.walkthrough: CASINOS without A and S leaves CINOS, which 'coming back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic relates to sound waves; a sonic speed is that at which sound travels.

clue.text: "Constructive play" destroying learner's self-confidence

indicators.note: destroying says a letter is removed from what is built

parts.note: Lego is the construction toy, so playing with it is constructive play
L is the learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: A quoted slogan, constructive play, that wrecks a learner's self-belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constructive play' sounds educational but names the building-brick toy LEGO, which loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is a person's sense of self-worth or self-esteem.

clue.text: Replacement of fossil fuels requires years longer to develop

indicators.note: to develop means the letters must be worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Phasing out coal and oil will take years more than hoped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to develop' rearranges the letters of 'years longer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Power from the sun is a renewable source meant to supplant coal, oil and gas.

clue.text: Senior nurses content to pay attention to her?

definitions.text: Senior nurses content to pay attention to her?

indicators.note: nurses means holds within, as one nurses a drink
the content of a word is its inside, everything but its outer letters

parts.note: to listen is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Junior nurses should be happy to heed the ward's senior nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as happy but takes ISTE from LISTEN, which SR holds. The whole clue also describes a sister: junior staff should listen to her.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward, whom juniors obey.

clue.text: Musical composed 32 pieces

parts.note: Chess is the stage musical by Tim Rice and the ABBA songwriters
set can mean composed, as words are set to music

explanation.surface: A musical made up of 32 pieces of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The '32 pieces' are not numbers in a score but the sixteen men per side on a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A full set for the board game has thirty-two men, sixteen for each player.

clue.text: Hide transfer of large amount backing special honour

indicators.note: backing here means coming behind, so the large amount follows the rest

parts.note: the king is one of the honour cards in bridge
a raft of things is a large number of them

explanation.surface: Moving a big sum into hiding behind a special honour, like a laundered fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb of concealment but is skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin graft moves healthy skin, a hide, from one part of the body to another.

clue.text: Coffee shop receives fine after distributing legal high

indicators.note: receives says the shop takes something within it

parts.note: a cafe is a coffee shop

indicators.note: distributing spreads the letters of the following word into a new order

explanation.surface: A coffee shop is fined after selling a legal high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after distributing' rearranges the letters of 'fine' before the shop takes them in; 'legal high' ironically names an everyday stimulant.
explanation.definitionFit: Caffeine is a stimulant drug that is legal and freely sold, so a lawful pick-me-up.

clue.text: Fantasise about following old man around yard in the morning

indicators.note: following puts the word for about after the father and yard
around says the father goes about the next piece

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad
re means about, concerning
AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Imagining things about trailing your father round the garden in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: To daydream is to indulge in pleasant fantasies while awake.

clue.text: Put back legal document containing deposit

indicators.note: containing says the document holds the next word

parts.note: a deed is a signed legal document
to lay is to set down or deposit, as a hen lays an egg

explanation.surface: A contract that included a down payment was returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' reads as returned but means postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: A delayed event has been postponed, put back to a later time.

clue.text: Chap is hungover, but not very drunk

indicators.note: drunk says the remaining letters reel into a new order
but not says that letter is left out of the word

explanation.surface: A man nursing a hangover without being properly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chap' looks like a man but is a verb, as wind chaps skin. HUNGOVER minus V is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold wind chaps lips, making the skin rough and cracked, so the verbs share a sense.

clue.text: Number one hit about America?

indicators.note: about says the whole string is turned round

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to tan someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: A chart-topping song about America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one hit' looks like a chart record; it is NO + I + TAN, which 'about' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: America, the United States, is an example of a country, hence the question mark.

clue.text: This plant's turnover makes phenomenal contribution

indicators.note: turnover says those letters are turned to run the other way
contribution says the word supplies part of its letters

explanation.surface: Business talk: a plant's annual sales make a remarkable contribution to profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like business revenue but reverses letters taken from 'phenomenal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anemones are flowering plants of the buttercup family, also called windflowers.

clue.text: Baby originally named by cracking joke

parts.note: né, as in 'John Smith, né Jones', gives a man's name at birth

indicators.note: cracking says the joke is broken open by the next word

parts.note: a joke is a good one, as in 'that's a good one'
at can mean by, as in standing at the door

explanation.surface: A baby given a name thanks to a brilliant joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like a first-letter signal, but 'originally named' is the French-derived NE. AT breaks into ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn infant, in medical language.

clue.text: Loyal soldier leaving base to avoid training?

indicators.note: leaving says that letter goes from the word

parts.note: true means loyal, faithful
E is the base of natural logarithms in maths
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A faithful soldier deserting barracks to dodge drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' suggests army service; here it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To truant is to stay away from school or lessons without leave, so dodging instruction.

clue.text: What is required to release 21 workers?

definitions.meaning: labour, the process of childbirth, with the force of it, delivers a baby, the neonate of 21 down
a nation's body of working people

explanation.surface: Asking what would free 21 workers from their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is the answer to 21 down, NEONATE, a newborn baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A labour force is the workforce, the people employed or available for work.

clue.text: Bank almost deceives punters by concealing weak holding

indicators.note: almost says the word loses its last letter

parts.words: deceives punters by concealing weak holding
parts.note: a poker player who hides a poor hand bluffs the other gamblers

explanation.surface: A bank that nearly tricks its customers by hiding its feeble assets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests finance; it is a steep river bank or cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a broad, steep cliff or bank, often beside a river.

clue.text: Try to contain love's soppy stuff

indicators.note: to contain says the try holds the next letter

parts.note: to have a go is to try
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Attempt to keep your feelings from spilling into sentimental mush.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is sticky matter and also cloying sentimentality, both soppy.

clue.text: Unknown speaker losing head suggests immaturity

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: losing head says the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a mouth is the organ one speaks with

explanation.surface: A nameless orator who loses his cool shows his inexperience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaker' reads as a person or loudspeaker; it is the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Youth is the state of being young, so a lack of maturity.

clue.text: Data Romanian sent back contains desired target

indicators.note: sent back says the hidden letters are read backwards
contains says the two words hold the answer within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Information from Romania, returned, that holds a sought-after objective.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'contains' into the definition; it is the hiding signal, so the definition is just 'desired target'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who is loved, the object of a man's affection.

clue.text: Lawyer's argument to remove barriers?

definitions.meaning: the case put for an accused in court
read as ..., to take away fences

explanation.surface: A counsel's case for tearing down obstacles.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal defence is the reasoning advanced to clear a defendant.

clue.text: Operations room where available guards are transferred to begin with

indicators.note: guards says the word surrounds the next part

parts.note: there means present and available, as in 'help is there'

indicators.note: to begin with takes the first letter of each of the two preceding words

explanation.surface: A room where on-duty guards are moved around at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' reads as security staff but is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating theatre is the room in a hospital where surgery is carried out.
